entries.line: About now has a What's new list of each update, and links to an Explore section land on that section.
Links can now open the map with City transit on, so a shared view keeps its trams and metros.

showMe.press: This link opens the map with Trams & metros already on.

entries.line: With City transit on, trams and metros now show when zoomed out, as city markers across Europe, and Warsaw’s trams are on the map.

showMe.press: This opens Europe with City transit on. Zoom in on a city marker to see its lines.

entries.line: On a small phone held sideways, Find affected railways in Countries and Speed in Explore now frame what they show.

showMe.press: Hold a phone sideways, open Countries and press Find affected railways.

entries.line: City transit now has 74 timetable sources: trams in Katowice, Łódź and Wrocław, and two tram networks in Barcelona.

showMe.press: This opens Katowice. Open Filters and turn on City transit, then Trams & metros.

entries.line: On a phone held sideways the map now opens on the whole of Europe instead of zooming far into one spot.

showMe.press: This is the view a phone held sideways now opens at.

entries.line: City transit grew to 70 timetable sources, 36 of them new, with Paris, Bucharest and Turin among them.

showMe.press: This opens Paris. Open Filters and turn on City transit, then Trams & metros.

entries.line: City trams and metros are on the map: an optional layer with 34 timetable sources, off until you turn it on.

showMe.press: This opens Strasbourg. Open Filters and turn on City transit, then Trams & metros.
